meeting_flow.opening_phrase: Hi. Everyone. How you doing? ... Thanks for coming on. I thought I'd start just by understanding a bit more about your current situation.
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: And then, you know, interesting short let. And then we can go through some figures in our service if it lines up with what you're looking for.
meeting_flow.income_intro: What I'll do is I'll share my screen and we can go through what we've estimated, the projections are and also where I think the gaps are as well.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: So we went through a bit on our call. I can share my screen and show you — so there's three things you'll have access to (booking calendar, Slack communication, monthly statement).
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: Discussion of handover logistics with the existing agent, transfer of onboarding data, and who at Stayful would manage the account day-to-day (Martin, customer-facing contact).
meeting_flow.close_phrase: It's been a pleasure. Have a good weekend and we'll touch base.
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: Lead-initiated: Rohana proposed the follow-up call herself once her husband had reviewed the email/action plan ('I just wonder... if we could do another meeting. My husband's usually home on Friday'). Zac agreed and left timing to her.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: So what do you think is the minimum we could achieve?
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: So I mean in your opinion what do you think we could project in the next year or so... we really need something tangible

lead_responses.what_lead_said: So you think this is totally achievable?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Yes — not easy, but definitely viable short-let over long-let; hinges on review velocity; backed with the Manchester case study
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah, definitely... that's what we're looking for — somebody proactive who can tell us what's going wrong

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Why aren't we getting the bookings?... June has been the worst month... a lot of the reviews are actually five star as well, so I don't know what's going on.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Possibly over-ambitious pricing without reviews to justify it; also flagged direct-booking potential from nearby transport/events/university/hospital

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Why aren't we getting the bookings?... cleaning issues... they've obviously not been doing a good job
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Rating 4.58 puts the listing in the bottom 10%; quality standard is high in this market and the management company isn't meeting it
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Husband's own anecdote: their daughter only books listings rated 4.8-4.9+

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How do you actually chase up reviews?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Persistence plus incentives, rather than a single automated ask

lead_responses.what_lead_said: We didn't see any surges in price for the Oasis concert last year — I just wondered how that works.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Could be supply/competition related; listing being in the bottom 10% means better-ranked listings get booked first

I mean to wrap a bit more around it. I think we've got a case study here for Manchester.
reassurance_phrases: This isn't a property issue that you're having. It's a listing establishment issue and it's a management company issue.

I wouldn't be afraid of the competition too much, really, because I'd rather go into a really competitive market that's got demand than the opposite way around.
emphasis_phrases: The key issue I would say here is getting reviews and getting the quality reviews
The two things that kill you are costs that are too high or you're not competitive enough with the listing
analogies_used: Manchester 3-bed case study (projected £62k gross/£32k net vs actual outcome) used as proof-of-model precedent
Friends'/family discounted bookings as a 'launch strategy' to fast-track five-star reviews
zac_language.numbers_framing: Always frames a three-point range (worst case / average / best case: £1,100 / £1,700-1,800 / £2,400 per month) rather than a single projected figure, and explicitly discounts the ramp-up period by 10-20% to set conservative expectations before showing the post-establishment upside (£2,000-2,300/month).
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Acknowledges the concern directly, reframes it as a diagnosable/fixable issue rather than disputing the lead's experience, then supports the reframe with a concrete external benchmark (industry review-ratio average, case study, or listing percentile) before inviting further evidence (asking for the listing link) rather than asserting certainty unprompted.

what_they_focused_on: Why the current company is underperforming vs benchmarks (reviews-per-booking, listing percentile)
Operational due diligence in meeting 2 (review-chasing method, cleaning QA, portal/reporting, contract terms)
what_they_needed_most: A specific, checkable diagnosis rather than a generic 'we're better' pitch
Third-party proof the model works (case study)
Reassurance that switching a second time won't repeat the same disappointment
what_fell_flat: No explicit statement of the standard 15%+VAT fee percentage recorded in either transcript, leaving commercial terms less concretely reinforced than the income figures
No firm answer on the Oasis-concert pricing-surge question beyond a plausible but unverified explanation
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: With EX-STL leads burned by prior agents, lead with the specific, checkable benchmark (reviews-per-booking ratio, listing percentile) even earlier, and proactively state the fee percentage and contract terms in meeting 1 rather than leaving it for the lead to find in the agreement — reduces follow-up admin questions and shortens time-to-signature.
